title: Fate Cards
next_chapter_hook: When Chen Ji held the first Fate Card in his palm, he suddenly felt an inexplicable thrill—the vague patterns on this card seemed to be resonating with the incomplete Tianji Record within his body.

text.content: Su Qingyao's fingertips trembled slightly on the yellowed pages of the ancient text. That momentary loss of composure vanished in an instant, but Chen Ji caught it all. He did not pursue the matter, merely casting his gaze toward the darkening sky outside the window, secretly noting this detail in his heart—whatever could so deeply move the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow must be extraordinary.

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji, at midnight tonight, the Rear Mountain Forbidden Grounds. Mo Xiansheng has something to give you." Su Qingyao's voice returned to its usual coldness, as if that trembling moment had never happened. "This matter is of great importance—you'd better go alone."

text.content: The night wind passed through the window lattice as Chen Ji watched Su Qingyao's departing figure. That word "alone" had been emphasized so heavily by her—clearly this wasn't merely a message from Mo Xiansheng, but also some kind of hint from Su Qingyao. He lightly tapped the desk, the Tianji Record Fragment in his sleeve warming slightly—the midnight hour, the forbidden grounds, this day had finally arrived.

Midnight. The moon hid behind clouds, and the Rear Mountain forbidden grounds of the Tianqing Sect lay wrapped in an eerie silence. Chen Ji walked alone beneath the moonlight, each step meticulously calculated—which Blue Stone could be stepped on, which thicket needed to be bypassed, which hidden mechanism would turn at what moment. In his eyes, this forbidden land was not forbidden at all—it was a chess game he had already seen through.

dialogue.content: "You've come." The aged and ethereal voice rang out from the void. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul slowly materialized from the first page of the Tianji Record, its gray glow appearing especially eerie beneath the moonlight. "The target for this scroll, you've completed seven-tenths. To unseal the next page of the Tianji Record, there's one final step remaining."

text.content: Chen Ji clasped his hands in respectful greeting, his posture impeccable in its reverence. He knew only too well this remnant soul guardian's temperament—every sentence only three parts spoken, the remaining seven parts left for him to comprehend. Mo Xiansheng drew three cards glowing with a dim light from his sleeve. The radiance flickered unsteadily, as if it might extinguish at any moment.

"These are Fate Cards." Mo Xiansheng placed the three cards into Chen Ji's palm. The touch was cold as jade, yet carried an inexplicable burning heat. "Three cards in total, capable of altering minor fates. Each use leaves a ripple in the river of fate. Remember—minor fates. They cannot reverse life and death, cannot overturn cause and effect. They can only pry open a slight deviation within established trajectories."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji brought the cards close to examine them. Vague patterns emerged on the card surfaces, resembling ancient runes or perhaps condensed landscapes and rivers. He suddenly recalled the records on the Tianji Record Fragment: "Sir, are there conditions for using the cards?"

text.content: Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul wavered slightly, his tone unusually solemn for the first time. "To use the Fate Cards, three conditions must be met—first, a medium, meaning a physical object or information connected to the target's fate; second, the object, meaning the thread of fate you wish to influence; third, sufficient fate thread fluctuation, meaning the target fate must be in a state where it can be pried open."

dialogue.content: "All three are indispensable." Mo Xiansheng's gaze pierced through the void, as if wanting to see through Chen Ji's heart. "More importantly, each card can only be used once, burning after use. And after using it, something called 'Fate Echo' will occur—the river of fate's error correction mechanism will be triggered, and at some point in the future, it will rebound upon you."

text.content: Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, placing the three cards into his sleeve. His expression remained平静如water, but his mind had already begun racing at full speed—Fate Echo, the rebound, three cards. This was adouble-edged sword; used well it could be a lifeline, used poorly it would be digging one's own grave. Mo Xiansheng said he had completed seven-tenths, then the remaining three-tenths probably connected closely to these Fate Cards.

Just then, the communication Jade Talisman in Chen Ji's sleeve suddenly grew warm. He took it out, his brow lifting almost imperceptibly—it was Ye Qing, that Holy Sect Saintess of the Demonic Path. He looked up at Mo Xiansheng, but the remnant soul had quietly faded away, leaving only one profound sentence: "The chess piece of fate has been placed. How to move it is your own decision."

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji." Ye Qing's voice came through the Jade Talisman, carrying a rare gravity. "I sensed three additional things on your person. Those are Fate Cards, aren't they?"

Chen Ji did not deny it: "Lady Ye's intelligence network is quite efficient. May I know what guidance you have for me?" His tone was neither indifferent nor intimate, maintaining his usual detachment.

"Fate Cards are no ordinary objects." Ye Qing's voice lowered several degrees. "There are related records in the Holy Sect's archives—after using the cards to alter fate, the river of fate will produce an echo. This echo will rebound against the user in some unexpected way within three to seven days. Minor effects include declining luck; severe cases..." She paused. "Severe cases attract the gaze of the Heavenly Eye."

text.content: Heavenly Eye. Chen Ji's heart tightened. This name was not unfamiliar to him—the occasional warning that flickered in the Tianji Record Fragment, the taboo that Mo Xiansheng spoke of with such reluctance. All seers throughout history had perished because of this. Could he, Chen Ji, be an exception? Ye Qing took the initiative to inform him of this matter—apparently this demonic path alliance was indeed developing toward deeper realms.

"Lady Ye specifically sent this message just to warn me of this?" Chen Ji took out the three cards from his sleeve, examining them carefully in the moonlight. The patterns on the card surfaces seemed to flow slightly under his gaze, yet the complete picture remained forever out of reach. Fate Cards, a lifeline or another trap? The answer to this question could only be known by trying.

choice.prompt: Three Fate Cards in hand, the threat of Fate Echo hanging overhead. What choice should Chen Ji make?

choices.description: Do not rush to use the cards; instead, find a very low-risk scenario to verify, confirming the cards' effects and the true power of the Fate Echo.
choices.visible_cost: Time consumption, may miss the first-mover advantage
choices.visible_reward: Gain safe experience in using the cards
choices.risk_hint: The verification process may expose one's whereabouts

text.content: Chen Ji tucked the three cards close to his body and decided to find an insignificant target to practice on. His mind raced through suitable verification targets—ones that weren't too important to trigger intense Heavenly Fate Resonance, nor too trivial that the card's effect wouldn't manifest. Suddenly, he recalled that in the Spiritual Fields of the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain, there were always several spiritual plants that would wither from various accidents...

choices.description: Since you'll have to use them eventually, why not strike while the iron is hot. Find a target with controllable risk but clear benefits, and directly use the cards to verify the effects.
choices.visible_cost: May trigger Heavenly Fate Resonance and attract unknown dangers
choices.visible_reward: Immediately gain combat experience with the cards
choices.risk_hint: The intensity of Heavenly Fate Resonance is difficult to predict

text.content: A dangerous smile curved the corners of Chen Ji's lips. Cautious? After walking the martial world for so many years, he had never survived by being cautious. He gripped the first card in his palm, feeling that strange sensation of cold and heat intertwining. Tomorrow morning, Inner Disciple Han Lie would have a sparring match with the Xuanwu Sect genius at the Martial Arena—that was precisely an excellent opportunity for verification.

Moonlight pierced through the thin clouds, falling upon Chen Ji. He stood within the Forbidden Grounds, the three fate cards in his hand glowing with a faint, eerie light. Mo Xiansheng's instructions still echoed in his ears, Ye Qing's warnings lingered in his mind, and Su Qingyao's unusual behavior today had left new questions in his heart. All of this seemed to point toward some grander chess game.

dialogue.content: "Fate Cards..." Chen Ji murmured to himself, his thumb gently stroking the blurred patterns on the card surface, "Rewriting minor fates sounds like a good tool for cheating. But this 'Heavenly Fate Resonance'..." He narrowed his eyes, a playful smile appearing at the corner of his lips, "Worth a try."

text.content: When Chen Ji gripped the first fate card in his palm, he suddenly felt a inexplicable throb—this card's blurred patterns seemed to resonate with the fragmentary Tianji Record within his body. The sensation was fleeting, yet it stirred an indescribable anticipation in his heart. The gears of fate have already begun to turn, and he, Chen Ji, is about to personally turn that most crucial gear.
